blocks.text: Here is a roundup of headlines from India on Tuesday, November 17:
PM Modi to meet Quad leaders in Manila
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi is expected to join the leaders of Australia, Japan and the US for a Quad Leaders' Summit and hold several bilateral meetings in the Philippine capital, Manila.
This is the first meeting between Modi and US President Donald Trump since the US midterm elections took place.

Modi and Trump are not expected to hold any bilateral talks on the sidelines of the summit, instead Indian news outlet The Print reported that a bilateral meeting is planned for next month in Florida, on the margins of the G20 leaders' summit.
Modi is also attending the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN)-India summit and the 21st East Asia Summit today.
Trump's ASEAN Play: The new front in the US-China chip war
At the ASEAN meet, maritime security, economic cooperation and development partnership are expected to dominate the agenda.

In his departure statement, Modi said India's relationship with ASEAN was "at the heart of India’s Act East Policy" and central to its MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions) vision.
"Our ties, rooted in centuries of civilisational exchanges, have grown into a dynamic partnership spanning trade, connectivity, maritime security, technology and people-to-people relations," he said.
